facts.activity_series: maintaining sealing systems on rotating equipment

control_failures.control_label: emergency isolation and depressuring on loss of containment
integrity of the mechanical seal support system

facts.hazard_release: fire, toxic exposure, corrosive contact, detonation
facts.title: loss of containment at TK-7103 during shift handover

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was medical treatment injury, with 1 person injured.

defences.finding: Control EMERGENCY_ISOLATION_ON_RELEASE: the emergency isolation and depressuring on loss of containment was never verified as effective, and the ICAM investigation classified this as an absent or failed defence.
Control SEAL_FACE_TEMPERATURE_ALARM: the seal-face high-temperature alarm and trip was never verified as effective, and the ICAM investigation classified this as an individual or team action.

Control SEAL_SUPPORT_SYSTEM_INTEGRITY: the integrity of the mechanical seal support system had degraded below its design intent, and the ICAM investigation classified this as an individual or team action.

recommendations: Restore the emergency isolation and depressuring on loss of containment on TK-7103 and record the critical control verification before this task is next authorised.
response.sequence: Work was under way in maintaining sealing systems on rotating equipment, specifically replacing seals and seal support fluid. TK-7103 (product storage tanks) is in service for export product storage. The task proceeded during shift handover while the emergency isolation and depressuring on loss of containment was never verified as effective. The chemical energy involved is held as hydrocarbon, and the recorded presentation was fire, toxic exposure, corrosive contact, detonation.
response.summary: On 30 January 2017 an incident occurred on TK-7103 at Cape Verity Export Terminal during shift handover, releasing chemical energy held as hydrocarbon.
